items.informal_name: Supremum of Image of Binary Function Equals Double Supremum
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} [inst : CompleteLattice α] {f : β → γ → α} {s : Set β} {t : Set γ},
  sSup (Set.image2 f s t) = ⨆ a ∈ s, ⨆ b ∈ t, f a b
items.informal_description: In a complete lattice $\alpha$, for any binary function $f : \beta \to \gamma \to \alpha$ and subsets $s \subseteq \beta$, $t \subseteq \gamma$, the supremum of the image of $f$ over $s \times t$ is equal to the double supremum of $f(a, b)$ for all $a \in s$ and $b \in t$. Formally, $\sup(f[s \times t]) = \sup_{a \in s} \sup_{b \in t} f(a, b)$.

items.informal_name: Supremum of Image of Binary Function Equals Double Supremum
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [inst : CompleteLattice α] {γ : Type u_8} {δ : Type u_9} (f : β → γ → δ) (s : Set β)
  (t : Set γ) (g : δ → α), ⨆ d ∈ Set.image2 f s t, g d = ⨆ b ∈ s, ⨆ c ∈ t, g (f b c)
items.informal_description: Let $\alpha$ be a complete lattice, $f : \beta \to \gamma \to \delta$ a binary function, $s \subseteq \beta$, $t \subseteq \gamma$, and $g : \delta \to \alpha$. Then the supremum of $g(d)$ over all $d$ in the image of $f$ on $s \times t$ equals the double supremum of $g(f(b,c))$ over all $b \in s$ and $c \in t$. Formally: $\sup_{d \in \mathrm{image}_2(f,s,t)} g(d) = \sup_{b \in s} \sup_{c \in t} g(f(b,c))$.

items.informal_name: Supremum over Binary Image as Nested Suprema (Right)
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_5} {δ : Type u_7} [inst : DecidableEq γ] {f : α → β → γ} (s : Finset α)
  (t : Finset β) [inst_1 : SemilatticeSup δ] [inst_2 : OrderBot δ] (g : γ → δ),
  (Finset.image₂ f s t).sup g = t.sup fun y => s.sup fun x => g (f x y)
items.informal_description: For a binary function $ f : \alpha \to \beta \to \gamma $, finite sets $ s \subseteq \alpha $ and $ t \subseteq \beta $, and a function $ g : \gamma \to \delta $ where $ \delta $ is a sup-semilattice with bottom element, the supremum of $ g $ applied to the image of $ f $ over $ s \times t $ satisfies $ \sup_{(x,y) \in s \times t} g(f(x,y)) = \sup_{x \in s} \left( \sup_{y \in t} g(f(x,y)) \right) $. This expresses that the supremum over the binary image can be computed by first taking suprema over $ t $ for each $ x \in s $, then taking the supremum over $ s $.

items.informal_name: Supremum over Binary Image Equals Nested Suprema
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_5} {δ : Type u_7} [inst : DecidableEq γ] {f : α → β → γ} (s : Finset α)
  (t : Finset β) [inst_1 : SemilatticeSup δ] [inst_2 : OrderBot δ] (g : γ → δ),
  (Finset.image₂ f s t).sup g = s.sup fun x => t.sup fun x_1 => g (f x x_1)
items.informal_description: The supremum of $ g $ over the image of the binary function $ f $ applied to finite sets $ s $ and $ t $ is equal to the supremum over $ s $ of the supremum over $ t $ of $ g(f(x, y)) $.

items.informal_name: Supremum of Binary Image Equals Nested Suprema on the Right
items.informal_description: For a non-empty finite set $\{ f(a, b) \mid a \in s, b \in t \}$, the supremum of $g$ applied to this set is equal to the supremum over $b \in t$ of the supremum over $a \in s$ of $g(f(a, b))$.
